doc.title: Carl Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, Georgia, January 4, 2013

title: Freddie Hubbard's hands-off leadership: learn the tunes from records
summary: With Freddie Hubbard, Allen had about five rehearsals in eight years; sidemen were expected to learn the music from records and never forget a tune.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: know, because, like I said, playing with Freddie Hubbard for eight years, his approach to running a band I appreciate so much more now than I did when I was in the band. Because he was not the kind of bandleader who was very hands-on. Like I think in eight years I was with him we had five rehearsals and three of those were for record dates. Because his mindset was we’ve got a gig, learn the music, and I’m going to call it and you just better know it.
How did you learn the music?
Okay, he was playing music from —

See that’s the thing. See when I was coming up, and I really sound old when I say that, Jesus Christ, but they quite often they weren’t giving you lead sheets. For instance, the very first gig I had with Freddie was November 12, 1982, in Greensboro, North Carolina. And we had a sound check that day, that lasted maybe an hour.
Okay. I just wanted to, that was cool.
